hints: For the greatest possible value of P, the particle is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping up the plane, so friction F acts down the plane.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find normal reaction R: $R + P\sin 8^\circ = 12g\cos 25^\circ$.
Resolve forces parallel to the incline: $P\cos 8^\circ = 12g\sin 25^\circ + F$, with limiting friction $F = 0.3R$.
Substitute the expression for R into the parallel equation and solve for P.
walkthrough: State the physical condition for the greatest value of $P$: as $P$ increases, the particle reaches limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding up the incline. Therefore, limiting friction $F = \mu R = 0.3R$ acts down the plane to oppose impending upward motion.

Identify the components of all forces acting on the $12\text{ kg}$ particle:
- Pulling force $P$ at $8^\circ$ above the slope: $P\cos 8^\circ$ up the slope, $P\sin 8^\circ$ perpendicular to the slope.
- Weight $W = mg = 12(10) = 120\text{ N}$: $120\sin 25^\circ$ down the slope, $120\cos 25^\circ$ perpendicular into the slope.
- Normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the slope.
- Friction force $F = 0.3R$ acting down the slope.

Set up the equilibrium equation perpendicular to the plane:
$$\sum F_\perp = 0$$
$$R + P\sin 8^\circ - 120\cos 25^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 120\cos 25^\circ - P\sin 8^\circ$$

Set up the equilibrium equation parallel to the plane:
$$\sum F_\parallel = 0$$
$$P\cos 8^\circ - 120\sin 25^\circ - F = 0$$
$$P\cos 8^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ + 0.3R$$

Substitute the expression for $R$ into the parallel equation:
$$P\cos 8^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ + 0.3(120\cos 25^\circ - P\sin 8^\circ)$$
Expand the brackets:
$$P\cos 8^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ + 36\cos 25^\circ - 0.3P\sin 8^\circ$$
Add $0.3P\sin 8^\circ$ to both sides and factor out $P$:
$$P(\cos 8^\circ + 0.3\sin 8^\circ) = 120\sin 25^\circ + 36\cos 25^\circ$$

Calculate the numerical values of both sides:
$$\cos 8^\circ + 0.3\sin 8^\circ \approx 0.990268 + 0.3(0.139173) = 0.990268 + 0.041752 = 1.03202$$
$$120\sin 25^\circ + 36\cos 25^\circ \approx 120(0.422618) + 36(0.906308) = 50.7142 + 32.6271 = 83.3413$$
Divide to solve for $P$:
$$P = \frac{83.3413}{1.03202} \approx 80.7555\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$P = 80.8\text{ N}$$
Thus the greatest possible value of $P$ to maintain equilibrium is $80.8\text{ N}$.
